title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the 2020 Committee report by outlining its strategy to improve public standards for artificial intelligence. It commits to enhancing transparency, accountability, and ethical oversight, and to developing regulatory frameworks that align AI development with societal values and safety requirements.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out rules to make sure artificial intelligence is used fairly and transparently in the qualifications sector. The guidance will help schools, exam boards and testing services follow best practices so that student assessment remains reliable and trustworthy.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems, looking at the legal and economic implications. It offers recommendations for policymakers and stakeholders on balancing creators’ rights with the need for AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, noting the need for stronger regulation and more investment in the sector. It outlines plans to boost innovation, safeguard privacy, and ensure AI technologies are developed and used in ways that reflect societal values and public trust.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the terms of reference and FAQs for a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards. It outlines the committee’s objectives, scope, and methodology for assessing AI’s impact on public policy and best practices.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into AI governance, offering its perspective on how AI should be managed. The submission highlights the organization’s concerns and recommends measures for better regulation and oversight of artificial intelligence.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will reshape the rules governing medical products, focusing on safety, efficacy, and ethical considerations. It applies the principles outlined in the AI White Paper to develop clear standards for developers, regulators, and users of AI-enabled medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This strategy sets out the Defence organisation’s goal of becoming a global leader in artificial intelligence by developing advanced capabilities, ensuring trust, and improving efficiency. It aims to make the organisation the most effective, trusted, and influential defence body in the world for its size.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright‑protected works are used to train and develop AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, highlights challenges, and offers policy recommendations to balance innovation with copyright protection.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan shows how the UK Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to make the most of AI, improving efficiency and safety. It also outlines measures to address the risks and challenges that AI could bring to the sector.
